editorial.headline: Private Work Training: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali at Higher Risk
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85579 covers privately run work-training activities across specialist, safety, career and technical subjects, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85579 is a broad home for privately delivered work training across subjects that range from training methodology and occupational health and safety to motivation, self-development and career development. Its scope also includes education and training for overseas or migrant workers, as well as specialist training connected with nuclear energy, radiation, radioactive materials, radioactive-waste management, and personnel testing diagnostic and interventional radiology X-ray equipment. The common thread is private provision: this is training designed around work, professional capability and specialised practical knowledge.

The activity is open to enterprises at every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That matters because the record does not confine this training activity to a particular business size. A small private training provider and a larger institution may therefore sit within the same activity, provided their work falls within its stated subject matter. The breadth of the scope is useful, but it is not a licence to blur its centre of gravity: the activity remains private work training, including the specialist fields expressly named in the record.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct. The activity is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower ownership ceiling in the record to qualify that national position.

Bali requires a more exact reading, but not a pessimistic one. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities island-wide. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The record places its Bali position at OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and explains that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. For a foreign-owned training business considering Bali, the honest conclusion is therefore clear: full foreign ownership is nationally open, and this activity is not stopped by Bali’s stated PMA moratorium.
